notes.title: GuildMestar Update 0.2.4.0
notes.content:
Hello GuildMestars,

Today marks the release of version 0.2.4.0! Not too much of this update is available yet but similar to the last update most of the work included here is for the big 1.0 full release.

Speaking of which, currently our goal is a full release around Q1 2025. There is still much to do but at our current pace we do believe this to be an achievable target. Some of the planned features include the full story of Phern, Steam achievement integration, and ideally controller support (though don't quote me on that).

As for what is in today's update the primary focus was adding some new life to existing story dungeons. New events have been added to most and alongside them you'll find a new rather vexing pest. The territorial Lastari have been spotted in growing numbers, especially around deeply forested regions. Be sure to deal with them swiftly as in numbers they can be quiet a handful.

For more details read the full patch notes below.

Signed,
StrangerTod - OffPath

[/list]

[list]

[*] Updated weather display on map 
[/list]

[list]

[*] Fixed a rare bug that would not allow old saves to be loaded after new unique or persistent dungeons were created
[*] Fixed a bug that would not allow drawing more cards than are in your deck and discard combined

notes.title: GuildMestar Update 0.2.3.0 - Item Tweaks
notes.content:
Hello GuildMestars,

It's been a couple months so here I am once again with update 0.2.3.0! If you missed the previous update here is a little reminder: Currently the main focus of development is on writing Act 2 and subsequently version 1.0. That being said I don't want to leave you with nothing so lets take a look and what can be found in this latest version.

Alongside a couple new event bases, bug fixes, and back end code changes, the update includes a handful of various item exclusive mechanics. In v0.2.2.0 characters saw an overhaul of their skill systems that brought new life to leveling. Because of this however trade items have begun to feel less impactful. To address this a set of completely new mechanics have been added at various levels of power exclusively to the item pool.

In addition to these new mechanics two (but really one) new NPCs have appeared! A mysterious creature now stalks the halls. Dressed in the vestiges of night's first light, cloaked in shadow, and swaying in purloined excellence, they lie in wait with feigned disinterest. Oh, and someone finally found the cook's assistant slacking off somewhere, and they have once again been enabled.

For more details read the full patch notes below.

Signed,
StrangerTod - OffPath



[h3]Version: 0.2.3.0[/h3]

[b]- Major -[/b]
[list]
[*] Added currently inaccessible additions to prep for v1.0.0.0
[*] Added 3 new mechanics exclusive to items: Burning, Expose, Feign Weakness
[/list]

[b]- Minor -[/b]
[list]
[*] Remembrance cards gained from allies deaths are now playable. This was changed to make it more clear when enemies were under the effect of remembrance, rather than taking little to no actions.
[*] Refined pathfinding code.
[*] Adjusted character collider offset calculation for hitboxes and overhead displays.
[*] Added Addy.
[*] Added a line to the Sum introduction quest referencing Addy's addition.
[*] Added various cursor states image to "Controls" section of the Help menu.
[*] Adjusted various door sprites in the Guildhall to better align with their surroundings.
[*] Added 10 new event bases. Note, any dungeon that can access these new bases will be re-generated on loading an existing save. 
[/list]

[b]- Bugs -[/b]
[list]
[*] Re-enabled the cook's server. Lazy Ndel forgot to pickup their shift schedule and thought that meant they didn't have to come to work.
[*] Fixed a rare issue that caused events containing multiple linked event options from the same sub event who all allowed advancement to be considered potentially unpassable and were therefore creating duplicate event options.
[*] Fixed an issue allowing multiple exclusive event options without specific parent sub events.
[*] Adjusted the GameMaster's idle animation to prevent them from occasionally standing on their stool.
[/list]

notes.title: GuildMestar Update 0.2.2.1 - Talk about Act 2
notes.content:
Hello GuildMestars,

Just a small little update today, so small I'm only considering it a hotfix. The real reason for this update is to talk about the size and frequency of future updates in relation to Act 2 and a small note on the game's price. Lets get into it!

This update really only adds one small feature, yet I feel it's an important one. I have noticed several people find some sections of the game less clear than I would like. Though they have been designed to be as intuitive as possible a little help never hurts. Coming in v0.2.2.1 a new section has been added to the quest book offering helpful explanations of various gameplay elements. While not all encompassing the information there should help those needing an extra hand and is available at any time via the Esc menu. 

And that's it for the update. Told you it was small. Now, moving on...

If anyone is familiar with the updates leading up to v0.2.0.0 (or lack there of) they may have noticed a wide gap when development focus switched. I felt full focus on the upcoming content was the best thing at the time however now believe differently. In the future though the main focus may be on a larger update I would still like to release, smaller, intermittent updates, generally expanding existing content rather than adding or overhauling. The plan is to ideally release one of these smaller updates at the regular update interval (every month or two). With that said I'm happy to announce from this update on development will start focusing on Act 2, and subsequently the v1.0.0.0 final version of GuildMestar.

Currently GuildMestar hosts a branching story spanning the landmass of Lorn and Phern's journey as a GuildMestar in the Calrian controlled continent. Act 2 will continue where Act 1 leaves off exploring the consequences of your choices so far and the fallout (or uprising) that occurs. In this major update expect to expand on the stories of previously met characters, make new allies and enemies, and take your shot at power with a new form of macro gameplay. This new act should be roughly similar in length to the existing Act 1, effectively doubling the game's content.

Now, as an additional note. When GuildMestar was first published in Early Access back in December of 2023 the price was set at $20. Looking back that price was too high for the current amount of gameplay offered. Starting March 14th the game will be offered at a 60% discount until April in which it will receive a price change from $20 to $10. I feel this price more accurately represents the game's state. As to those who have already purchased the game I can not thank you enough for your support and hope you continue to do so moving forward.

Signed,
StrangerTod - OffPath

notes.title: GuildMestar Update 0.2.2.0 - All Skilled Up
notes.content:
Hello GuildMestars,

This update brings with it a number of large changes to the game's skill system, completely changes the way the game handles dungeon generation, and adds a new type of skill for adventurers to use. Let's dive in!

One thing that never sat right with me was the chance that should you enter combat the initial situation could be so dire it would be completely unrecoverable. As the game previously handled combat there was very little a player could do outside the normal flow and as such it felt frustrating for the wrong reasons. Update 0.2.2.0 adds a new type of skill for adventurers, granted at level 2, called an Exert skill. These skills are special in that they do not get added to the character's deck but rather are available at any time via a new UI element on their exploration information.

The power of these new Exert skills lies in the fact that they are able to be used prior to the regular combat cycle and have powerful effects such as immediately drawing additional cards or granting Taunt. This on its own would be far too strong so they carry 2 heavy downsides: firstly they can only be used once per combat, secondly they cause you to discard ALL other cards belonging to that character. Due to these downsides the skill can still be used regularly but contains a strong level of strategic importance on when to best use them.

Adding a new type of skill shed some light on the existing skill system and while I liked the varying trees overall it felt... lacking. This update provides some much needed love adding altered skill trees tied to the number of overall skillpoints spent, passive upgrades such as increased stats and unique upgrades for each profession, auto granted upgrades for more basic race skills, and a complete visual overhaul. Having some skills auto grant level ups provides a constant source of power while the additional options in the skill tree allow for more diverse character specialization. Oh, and skill points can now freely be changed at any time, so go nuts!

On the dungeon side of things its more of a technical change but players will notice some interesting new additions. In the past dungeons were only partially seeded while storing some structural information directly on the save file, this is no longer the case. As of this update the entirety of dungeon generation has been seeded removing annoying save bloat and allowing for a lot of interesting alterations. The old system disallowed making structural changes on the fly and hindered the ability for dungeon mechanic and boast design, but no more! Additionally the map display has been overhauled providing information on the various rooms and routes available rather than just room depth in a dungeon.

All in all these changes give some much needed life to corners of GuildMestar and open a number of interesting possibilities in the future.

As always more information can be found in the patch notes below. Give the game a try and leave a review to let me know what you think!

Signed,
StrangerTod - OffPath


[h3]Version: 0.2.2.0[/h3]

[b]- Major -[/b]
[list]
[*] Full dungeon seeding and smaller save files. In the past only small sections of dungeons were seeded while the majority were saved and directly loaded.
[*] Dungeons can now spawn multiple room paths in addition to multiple progression options. A revamped map will display these paths before entering and during expeditions. Existing unique dungeons will still follow the old method of a single progression room path, though this may be changed in the future.
[*] Completely reworked the character skill system.
[*] Characters now have complete skill trees based on their Race and Profession. Each tier of the skill tree can be accessed per 2 points spent except for the first tier which is unlocked after only a single point.
[*] Profession skills have trees and branching paths as before however they now are spread between tiers rather than all available at the same time. Profession skills are also now entirely opt in.
[*] Race skills are auto granted based on skillpoints spent.
[*] Added a new type of skill called Exert Skills.
[*] Exert skills are granted automatically to adventurers upon reaching level 2 and are upgrade gradually thereafter.
[*] These Exert skills are uniquely different from normal skills in that they are not added to the adventure deck and are rather used asynchronously to normal combat. These skills can be used once per combat and provide the ability to make large power swings, however due to this they also cause you to discard all cards belonging to the character that is exerting.
[/list]

[b]- Minor -[/b]
[list]
[*] Changed the low difficulty double Du-urn fight to a single Du-urn. This specific combat was significantly more difficult than others at this level.
[*] Added a small new tutorial about characters and their skill points / exert abilities
[*] Adventurers no longer start with a skill point at level 1, they now gain an extra point at levels 5 and 10
[*] Added a new renown reward: Every 3 levels of renown new adventurers will join at 1 higher level (ex: at renown 3 new adventurers will join at level 2, renown 6 adventurers will be level 3, etc.)
[*] Added 18 new Event Options.
[*] Disabled the Action Block sliding animation at the start of combat rounds.
[*] Added shadows below characters to better differentiate themselves from the background.
[/list]

[b]- Bugs -[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed small black bar of exploration character portrait not highlighting gold when an applicable item is dragged during combat.
[*] Weather effects displayed in dungeons no longer load incorrectly on first entering a dungeon after loading your game. 
[/list]

notes.title: GuildMestar Update 0.2.1.0 - Release QoL
notes.content:
Hello GuildMestars,

Not too long ago GuildMestar had its first major release, and now to accompany it is version 0.2.1.0 it's companion quality of life update. Below as always you will find the patch notes but here are a few highlights:

Fonts across the board have been generally increased as well as the removal of a oft disliked cursive font. Almost every instance of text has been increased to aid with eligibility and certain headers have had new styling applied to better differentiate themselves against other text.

Dialogue audio has been reworked. Now no longer is the same sound repeated over and over while text is displaying, instead based on the letter shone a different sound will be played. Currently this new system offers the ability to make custom sound profiles per speaker however at this time only Phern uses a unique profile. Should this system be well received I plan on expanding this to add some additional character to popular speakers, and if this system isn't your cup of tea in the slightest, a new option slider specifically for Dialogue Audio has been added.

Cleaner combat UI. Previously in v0.2.0.0 the combat streak (now momentum) system was added. The purpose of this new system was to both speed up and add some additional complexity to combat overall. It however had the added drawback of creating a lot of clutter on the screen and I was dissatisfied with this. Now in v0.2.1.0 much of the clutter has been reduced and the information is better presented while not losing the original idea of the momentum display.

All of these changes are present in both the full and demo versions so feel if you are still on the fence about the game, give the demo a shot!

All in all I hope you enjoy these changes and look forward the to future of GuildMestar. If you have any feedback you'd like to give feel free to drop by the [url=https://discord.gg/EA9MMEVNsv]discord[/url], leave a comment on this post or the Steam forums, or leave a review if you've already purchased the game.

Signed,
StrangerTod - OffPath


[h3]Version: 0.2.1.0[/h3]

[b]- Major -[/b]
[list]
[*] Removed BitmGothic Font (fancy cursive font) and increased nearly (if not) every instance of text in the game, eye users rejoice
[*] Added new context sensitive cursor variants for hovering / moving dragable objects
[*] Reworked dialogue sounds to use a modular system rather than a single repeating sound. The new system should be more pleasant on the ears and offer a variety of audio experiences
[*] Added a Dialogue Volume slider to the options
[*] Shops can now offer items on sale. These items receive an extra discount but can not be traded back to that shop again that day
[*] Cleaned up combat display. Should be less going on and easier on the eyes
[*] Items no longer spawn conflicting mechanics (such as +1 speed to target and -1 speed to target). If this would happen now the effects are instead combined 
[/list]

[b]- Minor -[/b]
[list]
[*] Enabled hover effects for adventurers (could have swore they already were but when testing the new cursors I noticed they weren't)
[*] The introduction scene now uses the dialogue speed setting similar to quest scene dialog and the auto progression timer has been increased to allow more reading time
[*] Added additional dialogue to the introduction quest about accessing the quest log for help on what to do next and added a line explaining the momentum system
[*] Renamed the combat "Streak" mechanic to "Momentum"
[*] Adjusted character's trade opinion to make them a bit more forgiving at their initial opinion value
[*] Depreciated the "Haste" and "Slow" mechanics. These are now combined under a new single mechanic but for the player they should see no difference.
[*] Adjusted item display duration during combat due to no longer displaying individual stat icons
[*] Removed characters walking to center point during combat
[*] Added reload effect for when the discard pile is shuffled back into the deck
[*] Nerfed the attack value of "Bite" at its first two levels (4 -> 3, 5 -> 4)
[*] Added a handful of new item affixes 
[/list]

[b]- Bugs -[/b]
[list]
[*] Characters returning from dungeons now properly discard lingering applied mechanics 
[/list]
